description: Fix #1615: In the default (non-PgBouncer) deploy, Postgres RLS is non-functional because setTenantContext(no tx) sets a SESSION GUC (app.current_tenant) on one pooled connection that is released immediately, and each subsequent top-level db query checks out a DIFFERENT connection whose GUC is empty (further, pool.on('release') RESETs it). With the fail-closed policy this yields zero-row denials; without strict fail-closed it can leak. ROOT CAUSE: no connection affinity between setTenantContext and the request's data queries in a plain node-postgres pool. FIX: pin exactly one PoolClient per request (stored in the existing AsyncLocalStorage request scope), set the tenant GUC on THAT client, and make the global `db` proxy transparently route queries to the pinned client for the request's lifetime, releasing it when the request ends. This requires NO changes to the hundreds of route handlers that use `db` directly, preserves the PgBouncer path unchanged, preserves fail-closed behavior, and pins only one connection per request (no pool-wide serialization). Prove it with an integration test that fails-without/passes-with the fix.
steps: STEP 1 — Per-request connection pinning primitive. In lib/db/ (new file e.g. lib/db/request-connection.ts, or extend lib/tenant/request-context.ts) add an AsyncLocalStorage<{ client: PoolClient }> (or reuse the existing store in lib/tenant/request-context.ts). Provide: (a) `getPinnedClient(): PoolClient | undefined` returning the request's pinned client if any; (b) `withPinnedConnection<T>(fn)` that acquires ONE client from getPool(), runs fn inside the ALS scope with that client set, and in a finally block resets the tenant GUCs on the client (SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant','',false), set_config('app.current_user','',false)) and calls client.release(). Handle acquire failure by propagating the error. Keep this a no-op path when PGBOUNCER_ENABLED==='true' (in PgBouncer transaction mode the existing tx/session semantics already work; pinning is unnecessary there) so that path is preserved exactly.

STEP 2 — Route the drizzle `db` proxy to the pinned client. In drizzle/db.ts, when a pinned client exists for the current async context, the `db` proxy must execute queries on a drizzle instance bound to that single client instead of the pool. Build a per-client drizzle instance with `drizzle(pinnedClient, { schema })` (node-postgres drizzle accepts a Client/PoolClient). Cache the wrapper on the client object (e.g. a WeakMap<PoolClient, DbClient>) to avoid rebuilding per access. In the Proxy get() trap: if getPinnedClient() returns a client, delegate the property to the client-bound drizzle instance; otherwise fall back to the existing pool-bound getDb(). This preserves current behavior for any code path with no pinned connection (background jobs, worker, tests that construct their own pool).

STEP 3 — Set the GUC on the pinned client, session-scoped. Ensure setTenantContext(no tx) executes its set_config through the same `db` proxy so it lands on the pinned client. Because the client is pinned for the whole request, the SESSION GUC (is_local=false) now persists across every subsequent db query in that request. Do NOT change the tx-provided branch of setTenantContext (is_local=true), and do NOT change withTenantContext (already correct). Confirm lib/db/rls.ts still imports the same `db` proxy so the routing in STEP 2 applies.

STEP 4 — Wrap request execution so a connection is pinned for the request lifetime. In lib/auth/middleware.ts requireAuth(), the body is already wrapped in withRequestId(requestId, async () => {...}). Wrap that body additionally in withPinnedConnection(...) (skipped when PgBouncer enabled) so the pinned client is established BEFORE the first setTenantContext call and released after the handler completes. Do the equivalent for lib/tenant/context.ts requireTenantCtx() Server Component path — its setTenantContext + subsequent server-component queries must run on the same pinned client. IMPORTANT constraint to verify: the pinned client must remain pinned for the duration of the ROUTE HANDLER's queries, not just the auth check. Confirm how requireAuth's caller scope relates to the handler: if requireAuth returns and the handler runs OUTSIDE the withPinnedConnection scope, the pin is lost. If that is the case, introduce a thin wrapper the route handlers already funnel through (investigate whether there is a common handler wrapper; if not, the ALS scope must be established at a point that encloses both auth and handler — e.g. document that pinning covers the auth+context queries and add the release-time GUC reset as the safety net, and gate correctness on the pin covering the RLS-protected reads). Choose the approach that guarantees the request's DATA queries see the correct GUC; justify the choice in the feature findings. Prefer the smallest change that achieves correctness; if a global request wrapper does not exist, prefer establishing the pin such that it wraps the handler (e.g. via the existing AsyncLocalStorage already entered in requireAuth if the handler runs within it), and if truly not feasible without touching every route, document the residual and implement pinning at the broadest safe scope.

STEP 5 — Preserve the non-PgBouncer release reset as defense-in-depth. Keep the pool.on('release') GUC-reset in lib/db/pool.ts. With pinning, the client is released once per request (not per query) and reset on release; this still prevents any stale GUC from leaking to the next checkout. Add a brief comment cross-referencing #1615 and the new pinning mechanism.

STEP 6 — Proving integration test. Extend tests/integration/tenant-isolation.test.ts (or add tests/integration/rls-connection-affinity.test.ts following the same isDatabaseAvailable() self-skip pattern and cleanup pattern). The test MUST exercise the REAL app pool + rls helpers (import { db } from '@/drizzle/db', setTenantContext from '@/lib/db/rls', withPinnedConnection from the new module), NOT a locally-constructed bare pool. Scenario: (a) seed tenant A and tenant B each with a contact; (b) inside withPinnedConnection, call setTenantContext(tenantA,userA), then run a RAW read with NO app-level tenant_id filter (e.g. `db.execute(sql\`SELECT id, tenant_id FROM contacts\`)`) and assert every returned row has tenant_id === tenantA and tenant B's contact is NOT present — this proves RLS alone (app filter removed) blocks cross-tenant reads on the normal pool path; (c) assert that a request's OWN tenant context is visible to its data queries (the tenant A row IS returned). Add an assertion that would FAIL on the unfixed code: without pinning, the raw unfiltered SELECT after a no-tx setTenantContext returns zero rows (fail-closed) or leaks — either way NOT exactly tenant A's rows-and-only-those. Document in the test file header exactly why it fails pre-fix and passes post-fix. The test must run against a DB with RLS migrations applied; if DATABASE_URL is unreachable it self-skips (acceptable in-sandbox) but must be correct for CI.

STEP 7 — Extend unit coverage. In tests/unit/rls.test.ts (or a new unit test) add a test for the pinning primitive: withPinnedConnection provides getPinnedClient() a client inside the callback and undefined outside; the finally block releases the client and issues the GUC reset. Mock the pool/client as the existing rls.test.ts mocks `@/drizzle/db`. Ensure the PgBouncer-enabled path is a no-op (getPinnedClient undefined). These are meaningful (they exercise the new code path), not static assertions.

STEP 8 — Update operational docs. Update DEPLOYMENT.md (and any RLS/tenant-isolation doc) to state that with the connection-pinning fix, RLS tenant isolation is now enforced in the DEFAULT (non-PgBouncer, pm2) deploy out of the box; PgBouncer transaction pooling remains SUPPORTED and compatible but is no longer REQUIRED for RLS correctness. Note the per-request single-connection pin and that it does not serialize the pool. Reference issue #1615.

STEP 9 — Validate. export nvm; run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (zero warnings), `npx vitest run tests/unit/rls.test.ts` and the new unit test, and `npx vitest run tests/integration/tenant-isolation.test.ts` (+ new integration file). If Postgres is reachable, confirm the new integration test PASSES with the fix; then temporarily stub out the pinning (or run against the pre-fix commit) to confirm it FAILS without the fix, and record both results in findings. If Postgres is not reachable, document that the integration test self-skipped and provide the reasoning/manual trace demonstrating fail-without/pass-with.

STEP 10 — Commit on branch fix/1615-rls-tenant-isolation with message referencing the issue, e.g. `fix(#1615): enforce RLS via per-request pinned connection in default deploy`. Do NOT push or open a PR; the orchestrator publishes.
acceptance_criteria: A single PoolClient is pinned per request via AsyncLocalStorage and the global `db` proxy routes queries to it when present, with the pool-bound path preserved when no pin exists
setTenantContext(no tx) GUC is visible to the request's subsequent top-level db queries (connection affinity established)
The PgBouncer path (PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=true) is unchanged (pinning is a no-op there)
Fail-closed RLS behavior is preserved; the pool.on('release') reset remains

New integration test proves RLS blocks a cross-tenant read with app-level filters removed on the non-PgBouncer pool path, and that a request's own tenant context is visible; test fails-without-fix / passes-with-fix (demonstrated or, if no DB, reasoned)
New/updated unit test exercises the pinning primitive (acquire in scope, release + GUC reset in finally, no-op under PgBouncer)
DEPLOYMENT.md updated: RLS enforced in default deploy; PgBouncer supported but not required
`npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass with zero warnings; existing unit tests still pass
Changes committed on fix/1615-rls-tenant-isolation; nothing pushed
findings:
Implemented per-request connection pinning to make RLS tenant isolation functional on the default non-PgBouncer (pm2) deploy for issue #1615.

FILES CHANGED:
- NEW lib/db/request-connection.ts: AsyncLocalStorage<{client:PoolClient}> pinning primitive. getPinnedClient() returns the request's pinned client or undefined. withPinnedConnection(fn) acquires ONE client from getPool(), runs fn inside the ALS scope, and in finally resets the tenant GUCs (set_config app.current_tenant/app.current_user to '' , is_local=false) and releases the client. NO-OP when PGBOUNCER_ENABLED==='true' (runs fn with no pin). Reuses an already-pinned client for nested calls (one connection per request). Acquire failure propagates.
- drizzle/db.ts: db Proxy now resolves via resolveDb(): getPinnedClient() present => drizzle(pinnedClient,{schema}) (cached in a WeakMap<PoolClient,DbClient>), else the pool-bound getDb(). Preserves existing pool behavior for any unpinned path (workers, background jobs, tests with their own pool).
- lib/db/rls.ts: UNCHANGED (already uses `const client = tx || db` with the same proxy, so setTenantContext(no tx) now lands on the pinned client automatically). STEP 3 satisfied by construction.
- lib/db/pool.ts: kept the non-PgBouncer pool.on('release') GUC-reset; added a comment cross-referencing #1615 (client is now released once per request, not per query; reset remains defense-in-depth alongside withPinnedConnection's own reset).
- lib/auth/middleware.ts: requireAuth() body now wrapped withPinnedConnection(() => withRequestId(requestId, ...)). No-op under PgBouncer.
- lib/tenant/context.ts: requireTenantCtx() body extracted to requireTenantCtxInner() and wrapped in withPinnedConnection(...). No-op under PgBouncer.
- lib/client-logger.ts: removed 2 PRE-EXISTING unused eslint-disable directives (lines 41,53) that would block the --max-warnings=0 pre-commit hook (documented in FEAT-001). Unrelated to #1615; minimal touch only.
- DEPLOYMENT.md: new 'Tenant isolation (RLS)' section — RLS now enforced in the default deploy; PgBouncer supported/compatible but no longer required; pin does not serialize the pool; explicit honest 'Scope boundary (residual)' subsection.
- tests: NEW tests/unit/request-connection.test.ts (5 tests, mocks pool/client), NEW tests/unit/db-proxy-pinning.test.ts (3 tests, DB-free proof of routing flip), NEW tests/integration/rls-connection-affinity.test.ts (3 tests, live-DB proving test with isDatabaseAvailable() self-skip). Updated tests/unit/auth-middleware-require-auth.test.ts and tests/unit/tenant-context.test.ts to mock @/lib/db/request-connection (stub withPinnedConnection to run fn directly, getPinnedClient=>undefined) since requireAuth/requireTenantCtx now call it and there is no real pool in unit tests.

SCOPE THE PIN COVERS (honest, important): AsyncLocalStorage scopes are strictly lexical. The pin is applied inside requireAuth() and requireTenantCtx(), so it covers the auth + setTenantContext + auth/membership lookups executed within those helpers. Those helpers RETURN before the route handler (or Server Component page) runs its own later db data queries in the same function scope, and Next.js App Router exposes NO global per-request wrapper user code can hook (verified: no root middleware.ts request wrapper, instrumentation.ts only has register()/onRequestError, all ~routes follow `const ctx = await requireAuth(req); ...db queries...`). Confirmed the same lexical limitation already affects logger requestId enrichment (getCurrentRequestId() is undefined in handler code after requireAuth returns). Therefore handler-level data queries still run on unpinned pool connections; app-level tenant_id filters remain the primary scoping mechanism there (unchanged), and the fail-closed RLS policy is preserved as defense-in-depth and is now FUNCTIONAL on the pinned scope (it was inert on the non-PgBouncer path before this fix). Fully covering every handler query would require editing hundreds of routes (out of scope for this bug fix) or a framework hook Next.js does not provide; routes/pages can opt in by wrapping their body in withPinnedConnection(...). This residual is documented in DEPLOYMENT.md and the request-connection.ts header, per the FEAT-002 STEP 4 fallback guidance.

PROVING TEST / FAIL-WITHOUT-PASS-WITH:
- Live-DB integration test (tests/integration/rls-connection-affinity.test.ts): imports the REAL app db proxy, setTenantContext, and withPinnedConnection. Seeds tenant A + tenant B contacts; inside withPinnedConnection sets tenant A context then runs a RAW `SELECT id, tenant_id FROM contacts` with NO app-level tenant_id filter and asserts (a) tenant A's own row IS returned and (b) tenant B's row is NOT present. Documented fail-without/pass-with in the file header: pre-fix the db proxy always routed to the pool, so after a no-tx setTenantContext the raw SELECT ran on a different connection with an empty GUC => fail-closed => ZERO rows => the 'own row IS returned' assertion FAILS; post-fix the query runs on the pinned client that holds the session GUC => passes and cross-tenant row stays hidden. Attempted to run against a live Postgres via Docker (network OPEN_INTERNET); the sandbox's rootless podman could not expose the port (EHOSTUNREACH / cgroup 'operation not supported' / netavark setns errors), so the integration test SELF-SKIPPED locally (isDatabaseAvailable()==false), which is acceptable per the orchestrator; it is written correctly for CI where Postgres+RLS migrations are present.
- DB-FREE mechanism proof (tests/unit/db-proxy-pinning.test.ts): mocks drizzle-orm/node-postgres so each drizzle(conn) is tagged, and mocks getPool()/getPinnedClient(). Proves the proxy resolves to the POOL instance when nothing is pinned and to the PINNED-CLIENT instance when a client is pinned, and asserts `!== 'pool'` when pinned — this is exactly the assertion that FAILS on the unfixed code (which always resolved to the pool) and PASSES with the fix. This gives concrete automated fail-without/pass-with evidence without a DB.

VALIDATION RESULTS (nvm node v22.23.2): `npm run typecheck` exit 0; `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0` exit 0 (zero warnings, incl. the 2 client-logger warnings now fixed); full unit suite `npx vitest run tests/unit/` => 323 files / 5370 tests passed (baseline 5367 + 3 new proxy tests; new request-connection tests are counted within their files); integration files self-skip (no DB). Did NOT run `npm run build` (~5min) or full `npm run test` (times out) or postman suite (no live host), per orchestrator.

Committed on branch fix/1615-rls-tenant-isolation. Not pushed (orchestrator publishes).
